_note: All story text. Lines copied verbatim from the Figma frames; anything marked [placeholder] is waiting for the user's writing — do not replace it with invented plot.
house.commute: Alarm rings, coffee's ready, and the autumn air is crisp. You grab your coat and step outside. How are you getting to school today?
bike: You strap on your helmet and head down the greenway, pedaling past motionless highway traffic.
car: You turn the key and crank the heat. Off in the distance, highway traffic settles into a slow, idling crawl.
busInterior: You tap your transit card and board the Route 41. It’s crowded, but forty people are moving under a single engine.
lunch: You get a mid-day break and your stomach growls. Time for lunch. What are you eating today?
lunchPacked: You open your packed container from home. Zero extra plastic packaging, no delivery drivers dispatched, and zero food wasted.
lunchBuy: You walk to a nearby fast food spot and grab a meal wrapped in single-use paper, plastic, and disposable cutlery.
lunchTakeout: You order delivery on your phone. A gas-powered scooter arrives twenty minutes later, carrying your meal in layers of disposable plastic containers.
lecture: You're sitting in a afternoon lecture, and suddenly your professor calls on you to answer a question. Which of these is the largest direct contributor to global climate change?
answerAi: Though high-performance data centers consume massive electricity and water for cooling, they currently account for 2-4% of global emissions.
answerLivestock: Correct. Animal agriculture drives massive methane emissions and widespread deforestation, accounting for roughly 14.5-18% of global greenhouse gases.
answerUrban: Concrete and steel building materials generate huge carbon footprints, but overall it ranks just behind animal agriculture on global warming impact.
doze: You doze off. In your dream, a single afternoon in class scales up to eight billion people. Every collective habit ripples outward, shaping the world of 2080...
outcome.good: You dream of the world years in the future, and it looks like a utopia.
outcome.neutral: You dream of the world years in the future, looking just as it does now.
outcome.bad: You dream of the world years in the future, in ruins.
end.heading: fine line

endingReflection._note: Shown once, after the final cutscene and before the end card. {choices} is filled from the player's commute and lunch picks (each choice's `fragment` in choices.json): bad = only negative-score picks, good = only positive, neutral = both. One fragment: "X"; two: "X and Y"; first letter capitalised; none qualifying: `fallback`.

fragments.delivery: the food you ordered in plastic containers
fragments.fastfood: the fast food you ate in single-use packaging
fragments.packed: the lunch you packed from home

templates.bad: {choices} could lead to your world looking like this when we combine 8 billion people's choices. All it takes is one person to lead by example; you can start leading today.
templates.neutral: {choices} keep your world looking the way it does today. When 8 billion people's choices stay the same, so do the problems we face. All it takes is one person to lead by example; you can start leading today.
templates.good: {choices} may seem small, but multiplied across 8 billion people, they could help create a future like this.
